title: Active vs Passive Management in the AI Exchange Traded Funds
content: This study employes a sample of 25 active and 22 passive AI ETFs to examine a series of issues surrounding their performance, risk, pricing efficiency, persistence in possible pricing discrepancies and their impact on ETFs’ performance combined with the respective impact by the intraday volatility. The relationship between AI ETFs’ performance and market factors concerning size, value, profitability, investment and momentum is evaluated too. The results indicate that the passive AI ETFs have outperformed the active over their entire trade history, without however shouldering their investors with materially higher volatility. Moreover, both AI ETF groups trade at a persistent premium to their NAV. The con-current premium affects returns in a positive way, while the one-lagged premium is negatively related to return. In addition, a negative relationship between return and con-current intraday volatility and a positive (but less strong) relationship between return and one-lagged intraday volatility are revealed. Moreover, the majority of AI ETFs cannot achieve significant alphas. Finally, the market factors suggested by Fama and French (2015) and Carhart (1997) are quite capable of explaining the performance of AI ETFs.
